title: This game is good but it’s got issues
content: This game is fun, and I like almost everything about it, but there is just one major issue. When it comes to the rounds needed to drop big game in one shot you have to pay for them, no matter how good your shot is in most cases you might be paired with a competitor that has purchased these super duper rounds that are no match to even the best rounds you can get without spending and money, not to mention sometimes someone might have 4 rounds when you only have 3. And this is coming from someone who actually does pretty well in the game. But I just played a match and lost not because I can’t play well but because someone had an extra round and super duper rounds that cost $9.99 🤦‍♂️ give me a break, that’s like cheating in my book. Other than that it’s not a bad game, although you are hunting endangered species, and one I think 🤔 is even extinct. It would be cool if they actually paired a caliber with a rifle, and listed actual projectile grains, thus for someone who actually knows something about firearms might have the option to pick an appropriate rifle for the appropriate hunt. Also any head shot would put any of these animals down in real life even if it was a fairly small caliber at a decent range. But the point of aim and magnification in the game is pretty cool. 😎 anyways it’s not bad, not great. 👍

author: PalX007
title: Greedy, Pay-to-Win Mess Disguised as a Game
content:
This “game” is nothing more than a shameless cash grab. The title I gave it? 100% deserved. Why? Because unlocking decent gear without paying feels like trying to squeeze water from a stone. Technically, yes—you can unlock the better gear without spending a dime. But be prepared to grind endlessly for scraps while whales buy their way to dominance.

The in-game economy is deliberately slow, frustrating, and unbalanced. Every mechanic screams: “Pay up or stay irrelevant.” It’s crystal clear the developers care more about their wallets than providing a fair, enjoyable experience. This isn’t a game—it’s a microtransaction machine with a thin coat of entertainment painted over it.

The greed is disgusting. It oozes from every menu, every pop-up, every overpriced “bundle.” It’s insulting to players who just want to enjoy the game without being nickel-and-dimed at every turn.

Bottom line: Unless you enjoy being milked dry or crawling through a painfully slow grind for months just to stay competitive, avoid this disaster. The developers should be ashamed.

I have been playing for several months.
Game play is good. Mechanics are nice. Not bombarded with ads.

The bad:
The obvious pay-to-play strategy is pitiful. Allowing people to buy clips of 4 bullets when the standard is 3, takes the fun out of it, not to mention the skill. With equal equipment, 4 mediocre, not even great, kills earns devastatingly higher points than three perfect kills. It is a very unfair advantage.

The pvp matching system isn’t very good. The opponent usually has MUCH better or MUCH worse equipment than you. It isn’t fun when you’ve either won or lost before a match has even started.

Seems there are accounts that are hacked for the weekly ranking system. Within minutes of starting a new week, they have significantly more points than I will have at the end of the week.

Gets repetitive. The patterns of travel for the targets is limited. It is easy to memorize where they’ll go.

author: Ichabodto
title: “Love the Game, Hate the Broken Matchmaking”
content:
Really fun game, but the matchmaking algorithm has some weird quirks
Hunting Sniper is genuinely addictive. The core gameplay—lining up shots on animals across different maps, going for perfect headshots or heart shots, and climbing the ranks in tournaments—feels satisfying and rewarding when things click. I love the variety of guns and ammo, the tension of 1v1 PvP hunts, and how it captures that thrill of competitive hunting without leaving the couch.
That said, there are some frustrating quirks that hold it back. You can equip a clearly superior gun with better bullets, nail your shots, and still lose to someone running lower-tier equipment. It sometimes feels like the algorithm completely ignores the gear you’re using and just throws you into mismatched battles based on other hidden factors. I’ve had rounds where my damage, velocity, and accuracy should have dominated, yet the opponent pulls ahead anyway.
I really enjoy this game overall and keep coming back to it, but I wish the developers would fix the matchmaking algorithm so equipment and skill actually matter more consistently. If they tighten that up, it’d easily be one of the best mobile hunting games out there. Right now it’s fun… but those random “why did I just lose?” moments sting.
Recommended with some caveats—great for casual play, but expect some pay-to-win vibes and odd balancing in higher levels.

author: xILAGANx
title: Game Review 3.5 stars
content:
Hunting Sniper is a good mobile game to pass the time. The graphics are solid, the gameplay is simple and enjoyable, and the reward system keeps players engaged. The shop also offers useful items that can help improve the overall experience.

One downside is the long waiting time for chests, which can slow down progress. Another drawback is that the game only offers one main type of gameplay, which is hunting, so it can start to feel repetitive after a while. In addition, special ammo has to be purchased with gems instead of being available through coins, which makes it harder for free-to-play players to enjoy that feature.

Suggestions: The game would be better with shorter chest waiting times, more gameplay variety beyond hunting, and a way to earn special ammo with coins or through missions and rewards. Adding these improvements would make the game more balanced and more enjoyable for all players.

author: Fazemoneyyyy
title: Could be a 5* game…but
content:
The actual gameplay is great, but after the first few levels, its nearly impossible to unlock new animals.. you lose progress for losing a match, and at higher levels, you lose more than you get for winning! Meaning you have to win way more than you lose to even have a chance.  It just makes an otherwise fun game to pick up and play a lot more stressful than it needs to be. 

Couple ideas that would instantly make it 5 stars:

Take away the -trophy for losing matches so everyone can still make progress toward new levels. It would equate to ppl spending more in-game currency for higher stake levels anyway, so i dont really understand why they WOULDN’T do this.

Put an offline mode that allows you to practice on any level/animal. 

Thats it. Other than that, great gameplay!
